new_statements.relation_note: The catalog lists Ayta Mag-antsi with an empty rule and there are no existing statements; the dictionary supplies a placement: lexically specified stress, penult in most words, final in many, antepenult in a few, with minimal pairs. NOTE on the copy: the listed open_url (sil.org/resources/archives/45894) returns HTTP 404 (two attempts, with and without a browser UA), the SIL Philippines record for 45894 is an empty page, and the HathiTrust copy (mdp.39015063193695) is in-copyright search-only; what was downloaded and read is the SIL Philippines 2013 online edition of the same authors' dictionary, which the site says is built from the 2012 revision (Pallêkan Habi, 5178 headwords), not the 20…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The dictionary gives no prose statement on stress; instead every headword carries a syllabified pronunciation field with the stressed syllable in capitals. In the 113 single-word entries sampled (every 50th entry plus spot checks), stress is on the penult in 67, on the final syllable in 40, on the antepenult in 5 (loans and prefixed forms such as batiri 'battery', kaganawan 'all', mallêbah 'to wash clothes', mangkidal 'to creak', tsigmino 'to plot'), so placement is a lexical property of each word, not predictable from shape; the minimal pair lawak LA.wak 'plateau of tall grass' vs lawak la.WAK 'drool' shows it is contrastive. Penult is the majority pattern.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not marked as such; in multi-word headwords and hyphenated compounds each member carries its own capitalised syllable (bonak yabi BO.nak ya.BI 'midnight'; na.ma.HIG-pa.HIG 'to recover a little'; bunton hên pan sarili BUN.ton hên pan sa.RI.li 'to hoard').
new_statements.exceptions: Four sampled function words (a 1 'not', gas 'kerosene', la 'they/them', ya 3 relative pronoun) have no pronunciation field; one entry (hêyêm hê.Yêm 'damp') has malformed marking. No prose exceptions stated.
new_statements.identity_note: The online edition is labelled Ayta Mag-antsi (ISO sgb) by SIL Philippines, matching maga1263; Glottolog files the same work under the alternate name Mag-Anchi Ayta. No dialect is specified. Johnson 2006 (Ayta Mag-anchi reduplication, already held by the project from 2026-09-16, not in the works list) says nothing about stress.

audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation, the minimal pairs, and the sec. 2.5/p. 38 summary lines are all verbatim in the held Endriga & San Juan 2018 chapter at the stated printed pages 28-29, 37, 38. (2) The source is a 2018 university grammar sketch with a dedicated stress section and stress-only minimal pairs; Glottolog's 21-item bibliography and Crossref/SIL searches show no phonology article, acoustic study or fuller grammar for this language, so it is the best available. (3) Independent confirmation downloaded now: the SIL Philippines online Ayta Mag-antsi dictionary (Storck & Storck) marks stress per entry, with both penult and final stress and a stress-only homograph pair (LA.wak vs la.WAK), matching the 'lexical' coding; Johnson 2006 is silent. sources.quote: No prose statement reachable (intro page 404), but every entry carries a syllabified pronunciation field with the stressed syllable in capitals, and stress position varies by lexeme: penult in A.hê 'no', DI.la 'tongue', KA.nêng, LA.wah 'always', BAN.da; final in al.WA 'don't', pa.AN 'don't', tag.LOH, pang.ga.HAK; and a stress-only homograph pair lawak 1 LA.wak 'plateau of tall grass' vs lawak 2 la.WAK 'drool, salivate'.
